show.name: Paint & Coatings 2026 (Barcelona)
show.venue: La Farga, Carrer de Barcelona 2, 08901 L'Hospitalet de Llobregat
show.notes: Silitex is NOT exhibiting. Single floor at La Farga, stands 100–724 (official 2026 list, 151 exhibitors). This is a supplier-side show: most exhibitors are raw-material suppliers, distributors and equipment makers — paint, ink and adhesive producers mostly come as VISITORS. So: (1) visit the 10 producer targets below (mostly emulsion / polymer makers — defoamers in polymerisation and let-down), (2) meet the distributors as possible Iberian sales partners, (3) book meetings in advance with visiting producers. Free visitor registration: https://step-exhibitions.eventszone.net/myCongress/form.php?thisFormCongress=paint26&thisFormLanguage=en&thisFormCode=vis01 · Organiser: STEP Exhibitions Iberia SL (paintandcoatings@step-exhibitions.com).

top.what_they_make: Leather chemicals and performance coatings group, including water-based polymers and finishing auxiliaries for leather and flexible substrates.
top.why_silitex: Silitex has antifoams written specifically for tannery auxiliaries (DYNAPAN 301) and leather-finishing auxiliaries (CHEROX 100 I, BRILAX), plus DYNAWEED MS for acrylate/PU resins.
opening_questions: Which of your Iberian plants formulate leather finishing auxiliaries locally?
Is foam or micro-foam an issue in your PU/acrylic finishing dispersions?
Would you test a European-made alternative for a tannery auxiliary line?
top.avoid: Large global group with central procurement; Stahl also sells its own process auxiliaries, so position as a raw material, not a finished additive.

top.what_they_make: German chemicals group known for composite resins and gelcoats (BÜFA Composite Systems); it shares stand 136 with Ecoimpress, Kalfrisa and Renzmann, so which BÜFA division attends is not confirmed.
top.why_silitex: Gelcoat and resin production needs strong de-aeration; DYNAWEED 100 is a strong antifoam/de-aerator and AS 100 is a base for solvent-system antifoams.
opening_questions: Which BÜFA business unit is on the stand this year?
Do you have air-release or foam issues in gelcoat or resin production?
Who handles additive sourcing for your Spanish activities?
top.avoid: Stand is shared with cleaning/recycling equipment firms; check which division is present before pitching resins.

top.what_they_make: Italian producer of vinyl and acrylic polymer emulsions used in adhesives, paints and construction products.
top.why_silitex: Emulsion and glue production is foam-prone; CHEROX 703/704 are written for glues and medium/high-viscosity systems and DYNAWEED MS targets acrylate and styrene-acrylate resins.
opening_questions: Which defoamer types do you use in polymerisation versus finished glues?
Are you looking for silicone-free options for adhesive grades?
Who decides additive approvals for the Spanish market: Italy or the local team?
top.avoid: Shares stand 142 with Stockmeier/Intercoat, which distributes Vinavil in Iberia; Italian-to-Italian contact may already exist, so check before pitching.

top.what_they_make: Producer of photoinitiators and energy-curing (UV/EB) resins for inks, coatings and adhesives.
top.why_silitex: Ink and overprint varnish formulations need levelling and defoaming; DYNAWEED 201 and DYNAWEED MG are written for printing/flexo inks and overprints.
opening_questions: Do your application labs recommend antifoams to UV ink customers?
Is foam an issue in your waterborne UV dispersions?
Would a starter-formulation partnership make sense?
top.avoid: Mostly 100%-solids UV chemistry; compatibility of Silitex grades in UV systems is untested, so offer lab samples only.

top.what_they_make: Producer of water-based polymers (LAICRIL, LAITEX ranges) for paints, facade coatings, waterproofing, mortars and microcement; reports 400+ products, 39 countries and 3,000+ customers.
top.why_silitex: A waterborne-polymer maker that serves both paint and construction needs antifoams/de-aerators for emulsions and mortars; DYNAWEED MS is written for styrene-acrylate and polyacrylate resins.
opening_questions: Which antifoams do you specify in your starter formulations for customers?
Is de-aeration in mortar and microcement grades a pain point?
Would you co-test a hydrophobic additive alongside LAICRIL facade binders?

top.what_they_make: Global producer of emulsion polymers and specialty polymers for coatings, construction and adhesives.
top.why_silitex: Emulsion polymer production and customer starter formulations both use defoamers and wetting agents; DYNAWEED MS targets acrylic and styrene-acrylic resins.
opening_questions: Do Iberian application labs recommend defoamers to your paint customers?
Is there an open spec for a polymerisation defoamer at a European plant?
Who is the right procurement contact for additives?
top.avoid: Large group with global procurement; shares stand 321 with Vidara Spain. Expect long qualification cycles.

top.what_they_make: Italian developer and distributor of chemical specialties for building construction and monument restoration.
top.why_silitex: Construction and restoration specialties use water repellents and plaster/paste antifoams that are in the Silitex range.
opening_questions: Which of your products do you make yourselves and which do you resell?
Do you formulate water repellents for stone or masonry?
Are you looking for an Italian additive source?
top.avoid: Described as developer AND distributor, so it may be a channel or a competitor rather than a buyer; qualify first.

top.what_they_make: Producer of liquid polymer emulsions (Orgal), redispersible powders (ORP) and hotmelts, with about 200,000 tpa emulsion capacity in Istanbul and Rotterdam.
top.why_silitex: A large emulsion producer serving coatings, construction and adhesives uses defoamers both in manufacturing and in customer formulations.
opening_questions: Which plant, Istanbul or Rotterdam, buys defoamers for coatings emulsions?
Do you recommend antifoams in your Orgal starter formulations?
Is a silicone-free option needed for adhesive grades?
top.avoid: Shares stand 418 with Arquímica, Lamberti and others; Lamberti is an additive maker, so be discreet on the shared stand.

top.what_they_make: Spanish maker of water-borne resins (emulsions and dispersions) for coatings, textiles, wood coatings, construction and detergency, now entering adhesives; plants in Mollet del Vallès and Masdenverge.
top.why_silitex: A mid-size local emulsion maker is the ideal size for a flexible Italian supplier: defoamers for polymerisation and finished binders, plus a vegetable-based option for eco-label customers.
opening_questions: Which defoamer types do you use during polymerisation and in final binders?
Are eco-label customers asking for vegetable-based antifoams?
Who approves new additive suppliers?

top.what_they_make: Italian paint producer (since 1957) of solvent-borne, water-borne and high-solids industrial paints for metal and bodywork, with the MIROMIX tinting system.
top.why_silitex: A real paint producer running solvent and water-borne lines can use both the AS solvent antifoams and the DYNAWEED water-borne antifoam/levelling grades.
opening_questions: Which solvent systems (white spirit, acetates) do your industrial lines use?
Do you have cratering or foam issues in water-borne metal primers?
Who handles additive sourcing: the Aprilia plant or a central team?
top.avoid: Italian company exhibiting in Spain, probably to sell its own paints; it may already be approached by Silitex in Italy, so check internally first.
